canonical_statement: Scriptural texts possess a spiritual essence that transcends their historical or intellectual value.

attributions.surface_quote: Any scripture is only secondarily an historical document; it is primarily a spiritual message.

canonical_statement: The ultimate utility of sacred texts is realized through the engagement of spiritual consciousness rather than intellectual curiosity.

attributions.surface_quote: Its appeal must be primarily to the spiritual consciousness.

canonical_statement: Spiritual wisdom is categorized into ritualistic action for preparation and philosophical discrimination for ultimate realization.

attributions.surface_quote: Karma-Kanda deals with rituals... Upanishad deals wholly with the essentials of philosophic discrimination.

canonical_statement: The ultimate goal of wisdom is the destruction of the fetters of ignorance.

attributions.surface_quote: Upanishad means to shatter or to destroy the fetters of ignorance.

canonical_statement: Truths regarding the cosmic universe and God are accessible through direct revelation rather than human authorship.

attributions.surface_quote: Upanishads being regarded as direct revelations of God; nowhere is mention made of any author.

canonical_statement: Spiritual truth exists independently of its written record or historical origin.

attributions.surface_quote: No date for the origin can be fixed, because the written text does not limit antiquity.

canonical_statement: The individual soul and the ultimate divine reality are ontologically identical.

attributions.surface_quote: Tat tvam asi (That thou art) and Aham Brahmasmi (I am Brahman).

canonical_statement: The fundamental truth of the universe is accessible only through internal introspection.

attributions.surface_quote: the secret of nature lies open to us from within

canonical_statement: The unity of all life is a permanent and immutable metaphysical principle.

attributions.surface_quote: this principle will remain permanently unshaken

canonical_statement: The comprehension of metaphysical truths requires a state of mental tranquility and concentrated energy.

attributions.surface_quote: It is not possible to comprehend the subtle problems of life unless the thought is tranquil.

canonical_statement: Spiritual knowledge is fundamentally distinct from intellectual or linguistic translation, requiring direct transmission or commentary.

attributions.surface_quote: A mere translation, however accurate and sympathetic, is not sufficient to make the Upanishads accessible.

canonical_statement: The study of divine reality necessitates a preparatory purification of the entire nature of the seeker.

attributions.surface_quote: To study about God the whole nature must be prepared.

canonical_statement: Spiritual receptivity is contingent upon the internal alignment and peaceful disposition of the practitioner.

attributions.surface_quote: No study is of avail so long as our inner being is not attuned.

canonical_statement: The individual soul and the Supreme Being are ontologically identical.

attributions.surface_quote: Oneness of the Soul and God... are the leading themes.

canonical_statement: Action performed without self-knowledge binds the individual to temporary states of existence.

attributions.surface_quote: Works alone... must inevitably bind a man, unless through them he gains knowledge.

canonical_statement: The Absolute is an infinite totality from which the phenomenal world emerges without diminishing the Absolute's integrity.

attributions.surface_quote: From the Invisible Whole comes forth the visible whole... the Whole remains unaltered.

canonical_statement: The Absolute transcends linguistic definition due to its infinite nature.

attributions.surface_quote: God, who is infinite and unbounded, cannot be expressed by finite language.

canonical_statement: Phenomenal reality and the Absolute are fundamentally inseparable.

attributions.surface_quote: In the light of true wisdom the phenomenal and the Absolute are inseparable.

canonical_statement: All manifestations are modifications of a singular, unchanging, and infinite substrate.

attributions.surface_quote: all manifestation is merely a modification of the One Supreme Whole

canonical_statement: The perception of diversity is an illusion that dissipates when consciousness is unified with the Divine.

attributions.surface_quote: conception of diversity naturally drops away; because the One Cosmic Existence shines through all things

canonical_statement: Self-knowledge acts as the ultimate protective and sustaining force for the individual.

attributions.surface_quote: knowledge of our true Self is the greatest protector and sustainer

canonical_statement: Actions performed with selfish attachment bind the soul to the cycle of birth and death.

attributions.surface_quote: actions performed with selfish motive bind him to the plane of birth and death

canonical_statement: Actions performed as an offering to the Divine purify the soul and facilitate liberation.

attributions.surface_quote: actions performed with surrender to God, they purify and liberate him

canonical_statement: Post-mortem states of heaven or hell are temporary conditions resulting from finite actions.

attributions.surface_quote: heaven and hell is only temporary; because our actions, being finite, can produce only a finite result

canonical_statement: The essential Self is inherently indestructible and immortal.

attributions.surface_quote: How can the immortal Soul ever be destroyed? It cannot be destroyed

canonical_statement: Ignorance of the true Self constitutes the only state of suffering or 'hell'.

attributions.surface_quote: the only hell is absence of knowledge.

canonical_statement: Identification with the perishable body necessitates repeated cycles of death.

attributions.surface_quote: he who clings to the perishable body... must experience death many times.

canonical_statement: The Atman is omnipresent and transcends spatial limitations.

attributions.surface_quote: The Atman, however, is present everywhere.

canonical_statement: The Cosmic Self is the foundational substrate that sustains all life and physical phenomena.

attributions.surface_quote: all living things must draw their life from the Cosmic Self.

canonical_statement: The Self is simultaneously immanent within the individual and transcendent as the external universe.

attributions.surface_quote: It is within and also It is without all this.

canonical_statement: Perception of the fundamental unity of all beings in the Self eliminates delusion and grief.

attributions.surface_quote: he who perceives all beings as the Self, how can there be delusion or grief?

canonical_statement: The perception of diversity is a delusion that generates selfishness and suffering.

attributions.surface_quote: delusion rest upon a belief in diversity, which leads to competition and all forms of selfishness.

canonical_statement: The true Self is a transcendent, self-existent, and non-material entity.

attributions.surface_quote: HE (the Self) is all-encircling, resplendent, bodiless, spotless... self-existent

canonical_statement: Immortality is achieved by integrating both worldly action (Avidya) and spiritual knowledge (Vidya).

attributions.surface_quote: he who knows at the same time both Vidya and Avidya, crosses over death

canonical_statement: The individual Soul and the Supreme Being are ontologically identical.

attributions.surface_quote: the Soul and God are one and inseparable

canonical_statement: Reality consists of both the Unmanifested First Cause and the destructible manifested world.

attributions.surface_quote: he who knows at the same time both the Unmanifested... and the destructible or manifested

canonical_statement: Reality consists of a non-dual unity between the visible (matter) and the invisible (spirit).

attributions.surface_quote: no perfect knowledge is possible without simultaneous comprehension of both.

canonical_statement: The individual soul and the Supreme Being are ontologically identical.

attributions.surface_quote: The Purusha who dwells within Thee, I am He.

canonical_statement: The physical body is perishable, while the soul is eternal.

attributions.surface_quote: distinction between the mortal body and the immortal Soul.

canonical_statement: Perception of the divine in all manifested forms is the result of true wisdom.

attributions.surface_quote: he is able to perceive the Invisible Cause in all visible forms.

canonical_statement: Liberation from death is achieved through the integrated understanding of matter and spirit.

attributions.surface_quote: he who has a co-ordinated understanding of both... conquers Nature and thus overcomes death.

canonical_statement: Physical death is merely the shedding of a temporary vessel by the eternal soul.

attributions.surface_quote: death is nothing more than the casting-off of a worn-out garment.

canonical_statement: True reality is an indivisible, omnipresent unity; fragmentation is a product of limited perception.

attributions.surface_quote: We must not divide our conception of the universe.

canonical_statement: The individual self and the Divine are ontologically identical.

attributions.surface_quote: there is no difference between the Self and God.

canonical_statement: The individual soul is an infinite extension of the Infinite Whole, possessing its qualities when unified.

attributions.surface_quote: That which comes out of the Infinite Whole must also be infinite.

canonical_statement: Liberation from suffering and death is achieved by identifying exclusively with the soul rather than the body.

attributions.surface_quote: Transcending death means realizing the difference between body and Soul.

canonical_statement: The Supreme Being acts as a protective and unifying force for both teacher and student.

attributions.surface_quote: May He (the Supreme Being) protect us both, teacher and taught.

canonical_statement: Spiritual illumination is a result of disciplined study and divine favor.

attributions.surface_quote: May our study bring us illumination.

canonical_statement: The merit of a sacrificial act is nullified if the giver acts with expectation of personal reward.

attributions.surface_quote: The purpose of sacrifice is lost if the giver entertains thought of individual benefit.

canonical_statement: Giving with expectation of reward leads to unfavorable spiritual outcomes.

attributions.surface_quote: He who gives these undoubtedly goes to joyless realms.

canonical_statement: The efficacy of a ritual sacrifice is contingent upon the total surrender of the sacrificer's ego and possessions.

attributions.surface_quote: If he has vowed to give all his possessions, then he must also give me.

canonical_statement: A true state of spiritual sacrifice requires the practitioner to maintain internal tranquility and remain free from egoism.

attributions.surface_quote: a sacrificer, who must always be tranquil, uplifted and free from egoism.

canonical_statement: Human life is characterized by a transitory condition.

attributions.surface_quote: reminding him of the transitory condition of life.

canonical_statement: Shraddha is a complex spiritual faculty encompassing faith, self-reliance, and moral discernment.

attributions.surface_quote: It also implies self-reliance, an independent sense of right and wrong.

canonical_statement: The material form is subject to decay and rebirth, while Truth is the only immutable reality.

attributions.surface_quote: All things perish, Truth alone remains.

canonical_statement: The state of heaven is characterized by the transcendence of physical limitations, aging, and emotional suffering.

attributions.surface_quote: In the realm of heaven there is no fear... above grief.

canonical_statement: The guest is a manifestation of the divine and requires ritualized reverence.

attributions.surface_quote: A guest is the representative of God.

canonical_statement: The fundamental creative principle of the universe resides within the heart of every living being as vital energy.

attributions.surface_quote: It is hidden in the heart of all beings.

canonical_statement: Ritualized knowledge and action allow the individual to transcend the cycle of birth and death.

attributions.surface_quote: performs this Nachiketa fire-sacrifice... crosses over birth and death.

canonical_statement: Light or fire serves as the foundational element that reveals and sustains manifested existence.

attributions.surface_quote: fire is regarded as the foundation of all the worlds.

canonical_statement: The nature of post-mortem existence is a subject of profound complexity and uncertainty, even for divine beings.

attributions.surface_quote: Even the Devas had doubts about this, and it is not easy to know.

canonical_statement: Knowledge of the ultimate reality beyond death is accessible only to those who have transcended mortal desires and limitations.

attributions.surface_quote: The third boon could be granted only to those freed from all mortal desires.

canonical_statement: Material wealth and sensory gratification are transient phenomena that diminish human vitality.

attributions.surface_quote: These are fleeting; they weaken the vigor of all the senses in man.

canonical_statement: Human consciousness cannot achieve ultimate satisfaction through the acquisition of material objects or extended temporal existence.

attributions.surface_quote: Man cannot be satisfied by wealth.

canonical_statement: The essential nature of the self is immortal and undecaying.

attributions.surface_quote: undecaying immortal one

canonical_statement: Sensory enjoyment is transient and insufficient for the soul's ultimate fulfillment.

attributions.surface_quote: reflected upon the nature of enjoyment through beauty and sense pleasure

canonical_statement: The nature of existence beyond physical death is a hidden, profound secret.

attributions.surface_quote: that regarding which there is doubt, of the great Hereafter

canonical_statement: Human existence is defined by a fundamental choice between the pursuit of transient sensory pleasure and the pursuit of the eternal, spiritual reality.

attributions.surface_quote: There are two paths, one leading Godward, the other leading to worldly pleasure.

canonical_statement: The material world is perishable, while the spiritual realm is imperishable and constitutes the true end of existence.

attributions.surface_quote: One leads to the imperishable spiritual realm; the other to the perishable physical realm.

canonical_statement: Ignorance of the eternal reality causes the soul to remain trapped in a cycle of repeated mortality.

attributions.surface_quote: Thinking this world alone is, there is none other: he falls under my sway again.

canonical_statement: Intellectual conceit and worldly knowledge do not constitute true wisdom and can lead to further delusion.

attributions.surface_quote: Fools dwelling in ignorance, yet imagining themselves wise, go round and round.

canonical_statement: The human condition is characterized by a duality consisting of a perishable aspect and an eternal, undying aspect.

attributions.surface_quote: There is one part of us which must die; there is another part which never dies.

canonical_statement: Liberation from the cycle of death is achieved by identifying the individual self with the eternal, divine nature.

attributions.surface_quote: When a man can identify himself with his undying nature, which is one with God, then he overcomes death.

canonical_statement: Spiritual knowledge is not intellectual or discursive; it requires direct realization or perception.

attributions.surface_quote: What is meant by realization? It means knowledge based on direct perception.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality (Atman) transcends logical argument and intellectual comprehension.

attributions.surface_quote: this Atman cannot be attained by argument; It is truly known only when taught by another.

canonical_statement: Spiritual transmission occurs through the presence and illumination of the teacher rather than through verbal instruction.

attributions.surface_quote: the conveying of spiritual teaching does not depend upon words only. It is the life, the illumination, which counts.

canonical_statement: The ultimate nature of the Self is inaccessible to intellectual reasoning and can only be apprehended through a state of consciousness that transcends rational thought.

attributions.surface_quote: It is to be attained only in a state of consciousness which transcends reason.

canonical_statement: The eternal cannot be attained through the use of perishable or non-eternal means.

attributions.surface_quote: the eternal can never be attained by things which are non-eternal.

canonical_statement: The Self resides within the innermost core of the individual's being.

attributions.surface_quote: seated in the innermost recess, hidden in the cave of the heart.

canonical_statement: Realization of the Self results in liberation from the duality of joy and sorrow.

attributions.surface_quote: he who knows that One is liberated from the fetters of joy and sorrow.

canonical_statement: The Self is the fundamental source of all joy.

attributions.surface_quote: he has obtained that which is the source of all joy.

canonical_statement: Spiritual realization proceeds through the sequence of hearing, reflection, and meditative practice.

attributions.surface_quote: The aspirant must first hear, next reflect, then by constant practice realizes it.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality is the source of all desires and the origin of all joy.

attributions.surface_quote: Realization unites him with the source of all and the one supreme joy.

canonical_statement: The Absolute transcends the dualities of virtue and vice, cause and effect, and temporal progression.

attributions.surface_quote: That which is neither virtue nor vice, neither cause nor effect, neither past nor future.

canonical_statement: Finite language cannot fully express the Infinite, but symbolic sounds can represent the Absolute.

attributions.surface_quote: How can the Infinite be bound by any finite word?

canonical_statement: The sound Aum represents the totality of articulate sound and serves as the sonic manifestation of the Absolute.

attributions.surface_quote: Aum stands as the root of all language and the Sound-Brahman.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality is an eternal, unborn, and indestructible essence that transcends birth and death.

attributions.surface_quote: Self is never born, nor does It die.

canonical_statement: The individual soul is identical to the universal essence, which resides within the heart of all beings.

attributions.surface_quote: It dwells in the heart of each living being.

canonical_statement: Perception of the ultimate essence requires the transcendence of sensory input and the purification of the mind.

attributions.surface_quote: It cannot be perceived by the senses; a finer spiritual sight is required.

canonical_statement: The ultimate essence is the foundational substrate of all existence, encompassing both movement and stillness.

attributions.surface_quote: It is both stationary and moving, and It is the basis of all forms.

canonical_statement: The true self is distinct from the physical body, which is perishable and temporary.

attributions.surface_quote: The wise who know the Self, bodiless, seated within perishable bodies.

canonical_statement: The ultimate Self is not accessible through intellectual study or scriptural analysis.

attributions.surface_quote: This Self cannot be attained by study of the Scriptures, nor by intellectual perception.

canonical_statement: Direct knowledge of the Divine is contingent upon a process of divine selection or revelation.

attributions.surface_quote: He whom the Self chooses, by him alone is It attained.

canonical_statement: Spiritual attainment requires the prior purification of the mind, senses, and moral conduct.

attributions.surface_quote: He who has not turned away from evil conduct... can never attain this Atman.

canonical_statement: The Absolute transcends and consumes all dualities, including life, death, and social hierarchies.

attributions.surface_quote: Life and death alike are food for Him.

canonical_statement: The individual human experience contains a duality consisting of the Higher Self and the lower self.

attributions.surface_quote: The two signify the Higher Self and the lower self, dwelling in the heart.

canonical_statement: The Higher Self is the singular reality, while the lower self is a derivative shadow or reflection.

attributions.surface_quote: Higher Self is like a light and the lower self like a shadow.

canonical_statement: All external manifestations are projections of a single, unified reality.

attributions.surface_quote: all outer manifestations are nothing but reflections or projections of that One.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality, Brahman, exists simultaneously in both manifested and unmanifested forms.

attributions.surface_quote: He is manifested as the Lord of sacrifice... He is the unmanifested, eternal, universal Supreme Being.

canonical_statement: The state of immortality is defined by the absence of fear, death, and disease.

attributions.surface_quote: The other shore, being the realm of immortality, is said to be beyond fear.

canonical_statement: The human constitution is structured as a chariot: the Self is the lord, the intellect the driver, the mind the reins, and the senses the horses.

attributions.surface_quote: Know the Atman as the lord of the chariot, and the body as the chariot.

canonical_statement: The Higher Self is transcendent and cannot be defined directly, only through analogy.

attributions.surface_quote: The Atman is so entirely beyond human conception that it is impossible to give a direct definition.

canonical_statement: The Self, when identified with the body, mind, and senses, functions as the agent of experience and action.

attributions.surface_quote: When the Self is joined with body, mind and senses, It is called the intelligent enjoyer.

canonical_statement: Lack of discriminative control over the mind and senses leads to continued reincarnation within the cycle of birth and death.

attributions.surface_quote: He who does not possess discrimination... falls again into Samsara.

canonical_statement: The attainment of the final goal of existence requires the mastery of the senses and mind by the discriminative intellect.

attributions.surface_quote: He who possesses right discrimination... reaches that goal, from which he is not born again.

canonical_statement: The hierarchical structure of reality proceeds from objects to senses, mind, intellect, Atman, the Unmanifested, and finally the Purusha.

attributions.surface_quote: Beyond the senses are the objects, beyond the objects is the mind... beyond the Purusha there is nothing.

canonical_statement: The structure of reality is hierarchical, proceeding from gross sense-objects to the subtle individual Self, and finally to the Supreme Self.

attributions.surface_quote: Beginning with the sense-organs, he leads up to the less and less gross.

canonical_statement: The Supreme Self is the ultimate, non-transcendent reality beyond which no higher principle exists.

attributions.surface_quote: Above this is the Purusha or Supreme Self. Than this there is nothing higher.

canonical_statement: The Self is omnipresent in all beings but remains hidden from ordinary perception due to cognitive distraction.

attributions.surface_quote: Atman, hidden in all beings, does not shine forth; but It is seen by subtle seers.

canonical_statement: Realization of the Supreme Self requires the systematic subordination of sensory and mental faculties to higher intelligence.

attributions.surface_quote: Control speech by mind, mind by intellect, intellect by the great Atman.

canonical_statement: Direct transmission of truth from an illumined teacher is necessary for the realization of the Supreme.

attributions.surface_quote: Seek out those who know the Truth, because only those who have direct vision are capable of teaching.

canonical_statement: The ultimate essence of being is formless, eternal, immutable, and transcends sensory perception.

attributions.surface_quote: That which is soundless, touchless, formless, undecaying; also tasteless, odorless, and eternal.

canonical_statement: Immortality is a state of consciousness achieved by detaching from name, form, and perishable objects.

attributions.surface_quote: Immortality is a state of consciousness and is not gained by clinging to form.

canonical_statement: The individual self (Atman) is distinct from the physical form, which is subject to death.

attributions.surface_quote: What dies? Form. Therefore the formful man dies; but not that which dwells within.

canonical_statement: Human perception is naturally oriented toward the external, which obscures the vision of the inner Self.

attributions.surface_quote: Man's mind is constantly drawn outward through the channels of his senses.

canonical_statement: The realization of the inner Self requires a deliberate withdrawal of attention from external phenomena.

attributions.surface_quote: Some wise man, however, desiring immortality, with eyes turned away sees the Atman within.

canonical_statement: The phenomenal world is characterized by transience and is distinct from the permanent reality.

attributions.surface_quote: distinguish between real and unreal, the fleeting and the permanent

canonical_statement: Suffering arises from the misidentification of the self with transient, mortal forms.

attributions.surface_quote: identify themselves with that which is born and which dies

canonical_statement: The Self (Atman) is the necessary substrate for all perception, knowledge, and states of consciousness.

attributions.surface_quote: all knowledge... is possible only because the Self exists

canonical_statement: The Atman is the transcendent lord of time, existing as the perceiver of past and future.

attributions.surface_quote: lord of the past and future

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality (Brahman/Atman) precedes the manifestation of the material elements.

attributions.surface_quote: He existed before the first evolution of the five elements

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality (Brahman) is the singular substrate underlying all existence and divine beings.

attributions.surface_quote: From whence the sun rises, and whither it goes, upon That all the Devas depend.

canonical_statement: The perception of duality between the visible and invisible realms is an illusion that perpetuates the cycle of death.

attributions.surface_quote: He who sees difference between visible and invisible goes from death to death.

canonical_statement: Ultimate reality cannot be apprehended through sensory perception but is realized through the purified mind.

attributions.surface_quote: This knowledge cannot be acquired through sense-perception; it can only be attained by the purified mind.

canonical_statement: The Self (Purusha) is an eternal, unchanging essence that transcends temporal progression.

attributions.surface_quote: Purusha resides in the middle of the body as the lord of the past and the future.

canonical_statement: The infinite Self appears localized within the physical body, specifically the heart, to facilitate human experience.

attributions.surface_quote: Although It is limitless and all-pervading, yet in relation to Its abiding-place It is represented as limited.

canonical_statement: The Soul possesses an inherent, unchanging, and luminous nature.

attributions.surface_quote: the Soul, whose light is pure like a flame without smoke.

canonical_statement: Death involves no ontological change to the Soul, as it remains eternally identical.

attributions.surface_quote: no real change takes place, because the Soul is ever the same.

canonical_statement: Perceiving multiplicity in the phenomenal world causes the consciousness to become fragmented and scattered.

attributions.surface_quote: he who sees difference runs after them in various directions.

canonical_statement: The individual Self of an enlightened being merges into and becomes identical with the Supreme Reality.

attributions.surface_quote: pure water poured into pure water becomes one

canonical_statement: The individual human body is a vessel for the eternal, unchanging, and unborn Spirit.

attributions.surface_quote: The eternal unborn Spirit dwells in the human body.

canonical_statement: The Self (Atman) is ontologically distinct from the physical body and remains unaffected by biological processes.

attributions.surface_quote: The Self is not affected by the changes of the physical organism.

canonical_statement: The Supreme Spirit is the singular, omnipresent essence underlying all manifestations in the universe.

attributions.surface_quote: He dwells in man, in space, in water, in earth, in mountains.

canonical_statement: Biological life is sustained not by breath itself, but by a deeper, underlying principle upon which breath depends.

attributions.surface_quote: No mortal lives by breath, but by another on which these two depend.

canonical_statement: The trajectory of the soul after death is determined by the causal influence of past deeds and knowledge.

attributions.surface_quote: Jivas enter wombs or immovable forms according to their deeds and knowledge.

canonical_statement: The Atman is a singular essence that takes on diverse forms based on the medium it inhabits.

attributions.surface_quote: As fire becomes various according to what it burns, so does the Atman.

canonical_statement: The singular, formless Self manifests as multiplicity by entering into various forms while simultaneously remaining transcendent and external to those forms.

attributions.surface_quote: though one, become various according to what it enters. It also exists outside.

canonical_statement: The essential Self remains fundamentally unaffected and uncontaminated by the suffering or impurities of the physical forms it inhabits.

attributions.surface_quote: the Divine Self within is not touched by the impurity or suffering of the physical form

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality is the singular source of consciousness that fulfills the desires of all beings.

attributions.surface_quote: the eternal consciousness of the conscious, who, though one, fulfils the desires of many

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality is self-luminous and serves as the source of light for all phenomena in the universe.

attributions.surface_quote: When He shines, everything shines after Him; by His light all is lighted.

canonical_statement: The phenomenal universe originates from and is supported by an unchanging, transcendent absolute reality.

attributions.chapter: Part — ancient Aswattha tree has its root
attributions.surface_quote: All the worlds rest in That. There is nothing beyond Him.

canonical_statement: All natural forces and cosmic entities operate under the absolute, inevitable law of the Supreme.

attributions.chapter: Part — ancient Aswattha tree has its root
attributions.surface_quote: From fear of Him the fire burns, from fear of Him the sun shines.

canonical_statement: Reincarnation is the consequence of failing to realize the nature of the Supreme before physical death.

attributions.chapter: Part — ancient Aswattha tree has its root
attributions.surface_quote: If a man is not able to know Him before the dissolution of the body, he becomes embodied again.

canonical_statement: The Supreme is perceived differently depending on the level of consciousness or the realm of experience.

attributions.chapter: Part — ancient Aswattha tree has its root
attributions.surface_quote: As a mirror, so is He seen within oneself; as in a dream, so in the world of the fathers.

canonical_statement: Individual existence is entirely dependent on the Supreme, analogous to the body's dependence on the soul.

attributions.chapter: Part — ancient Aswattha tree has its root
attributions.surface_quote: Nothing in the created world can exist independent of Brahman.

canonical_statement: The Atman is an eternal, birthless, and deathless entity distinct from the transient physical senses and body.

attributions.chapter: Part — ancient Aswattha tree has its root
attributions.surface_quote: Atman, which is birthless and deathless, with that which has beginning and end.

canonical_statement: There exists a hierarchical structure of reality ascending from senses to mind, intellect, Atman, the Unmanifested, and finally the Purusha.

attributions.chapter: Part — ancient Aswattha tree has its root
attributions.surface_quote: higher than the mind is the intellect, higher than the intellect is the great Atman.

canonical_statement: The Absolute is formless and imperceptible to the senses, accessible only through the refinement of internal faculties.

attributions.chapter: Part — ancient Aswattha tree has its root
attributions.surface_quote: The Supreme, being formless, cannot be discerned by the senses.

canonical_statement: The highest state of consciousness is achieved by the cessation of sensory and intellectual activity through meditative withdrawal.

attributions.chapter: Part — ancient Aswattha tree has its root
attributions.surface_quote: When the five organs of perception become still... that is called the highest state.

canonical_statement: Yoga is the process of uniting the lower self with the Higher Self by withdrawing forces from external objects.

attributions.chapter: Part — ancient Aswattha tree has its root
attributions.surface_quote: Yoga comes and goes... means to join or to unite the lower self with the Higher Self.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality is inaccessible to sensory perception and intellectual cognition.

attributions.chapter: Part — ancient Aswattha tree has its root
attributions.surface_quote: HE cannot be attained by speech, by mind, or by the eye.

canonical_statement: The Divine exists as the singular reality underlying both the manifest and unmanifest realms.

attributions.chapter: Part — ancient Aswattha tree has its root
attributions.surface_quote: He alone exists in both the visible and the invisible world.

canonical_statement: Immortality is achieved through the cessation of all worldly desires and the dissolution of emotional attachments.

attributions.chapter: Part — ancient Aswattha tree has its root
attributions.surface_quote: When all the ties of the heart are cut asunder here, then the mortal becomes immortal.

canonical_statement: The direction of the mind's post-mortem trajectory is determined by the nature of its desires.

attributions.chapter: Part — ancient Aswattha tree has its root
attributions.surface_quote: The direction in which it moves is determined by its desires and tendencies.

canonical_statement: The individual Self is a distinct, deathless entity residing within the physical heart.

attributions.chapter: Part — ancient Aswattha tree has its root
attributions.surface_quote: The inner Self, is ever seated in the heart of all living beings.

canonical_statement: The Soul can be experientially separated from the physical body through disciplined discrimination.

attributions.chapter: Part — ancient Aswattha tree has its root
attributions.surface_quote: One should learn to differentiate the Soul from the body.

canonical_statement: The attainment of knowledge regarding the nature of the Self results in liberation from mortality and impurity.

attributions.chapter: Part — ancient Aswattha tree has its root
attributions.surface_quote: knows the nature of the Self... became free from impurity and death

canonical_statement: The realization of the Self is equivalent to the attainment of the Supreme Reality (Brahman).

attributions.chapter: Part — ancient Aswattha tree has its root
attributions.surface_quote: knows the nature of the Self... attained Brahman

canonical_statement: Spiritual practice (Yoga) serves as a necessary methodology for achieving metaphysical liberation.

attributions.chapter: Part — ancient Aswattha tree has its root
attributions.surface_quote: together with all the rules of Yoga, became free

canonical_statement: Individual self-consciousness is capable of expanding until it becomes identical with the Supreme Consciousness.

attributions.surface_quote: expand his self-consciousness until it has become identical with God-Consciousness.

canonical_statement: The totality of individual existence, including physical faculties and life-force, is fundamentally identical to the Supreme Being (Brahman).

attributions.surface_quote: All is the Brahman (Supreme Lord) of the Upanishads.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality is the source of all individual faculties and sensory perceptions.

attributions.surface_quote: All my limbs, speech, hearing, strength and all senses, gain in vigor. All is the Brahman.

canonical_statement: The sensory and cognitive faculties are animated by a singular, transcendent, and invisible causal principle.

attributions.surface_quote: It is the ear of the ear, the mind of the mind.

canonical_statement: Human mortality is a consequence of identifying exclusively with the physical form and sensory experience.

attributions.surface_quote: He is completely identified with his external nature.

canonical_statement: Immortality is achieved by transcending the physical nature and realizing the eternal essence within.

attributions.surface_quote: Immortality is attained when man transcends his apparent nature.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality is beyond the reach of sensory perception, finite language, and intellectual comprehension.

attributions.surface_quote: It is distinct from the known and also It is beyond the unknown.

canonical_statement: The Absolute is beyond the reach of finite sensory perception and intellectual comprehension.

attributions.surface_quote: He is unknowable to man's finite nature.

canonical_statement: The Absolute is the underlying substrate that enables the function of all sensory and mental faculties.

attributions.surface_quote: That by which the eye is able to see: know that alone to be the Brahman.

canonical_statement: There exists a fourth state of consciousness, the superconscious, which transcends waking, dreaming, and sleeping.

attributions.surface_quote: There is, however, a fourth state, the superconscious, which transcends these.

canonical_statement: The Absolute can only be apprehended when the mind is purified and illumined by Cosmic Intelligence.

attributions.surface_quote: He can be known, however, by the purified mind only.

canonical_statement: The claim of intellectual mastery over the Absolute is evidence of ignorance regarding its true nature.

attributions.surface_quote: If thou thinkest 'I know It well,' then it is certain that thou knowest but little.

canonical_statement: True knowledge of the ultimate reality requires direct experiential union rather than intellectual recognition.

attributions.surface_quote: Mere intellectual recognition will not give you true knowledge of It.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality, Brahman, transcends the reach of sensory perception, speech, and the mind.

attributions.surface_quote: There the eye does not go, nor speech, nor mind.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality is simultaneously beyond the known and the unknown, rendering standard definitions of knowledge inapplicable.

attributions.surface_quote: That is distinct from known and also It is beyond the unknown.

canonical_statement: Individual existence is derived from the ultimate reality, providing an inherent, non-phenomenal link to it.

attributions.surface_quote: The very fact that I exist... shows that I know; for It is the source.

canonical_statement: Attainment of soul-consciousness necessitates transcending the material realm and relative, phenomenal knowledge.

attributions.surface_quote: One who wishes to attain Soul-consciousness must rise above matter.

canonical_statement: Material science is inherently limited because it relies exclusively on sense perception.

attributions.surface_quote: Material science being confined to the sense plane, it ignores what is beyond.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality (Brahman) is beyond the reach of mind, speech, and sense perception.

attributions.surface_quote: Brahman is unthinkable, because unconditioned.

canonical_statement: True knowledge of the Infinite is characterized by the recognition of its unknowability.

attributions.surface_quote: The true knowers think they can never know It.

canonical_statement: The true Self is the underlying subject that enables perception, rather than the object of perception.

attributions.surface_quote: The real Self is that within by which he hears and speaks and sees.

canonical_statement: Immortality is attained through the realization of the Self as the basis of all states of consciousness.

attributions.surface_quote: Brahman is known, when It is known in every state of consciousness.

canonical_statement: The essence of the individual remains untouched by the decay and death of the physical body.

attributions.surface_quote: Although his body may decay and die, the subtle essence of his being remains untouched.

canonical_statement: Individual power derived from physical or mental faculties is finite and cannot overcome death.

attributions.surface_quote: strength which comes from one's own muscle and brain... must be limited and mortal

canonical_statement: Immortality is attained through the direct experiential knowledge of the undying Self (Atman).

attributions.surface_quote: through the strength which Atma-gndna or Self-knowledge immortality is reached

canonical_statement: The Absolute (Brahman) is the singular, non-personal, and inexhaustible source of all manifested existence.

attributions.surface_quote: Brahman is the Absolute, the One without a second, the essence of all.

canonical_statement: All manifested forms are dependent on the Absolute and lack independent existence, similar to waves in an ocean.

attributions.surface_quote: No manifested form of life can be independent of its source

canonical_statement: The Absolute is the sole agent of all action; individual claims to agency are illusory.

attributions.surface_quote: Nothing moves without that Power. He is the only Doer.

canonical_statement: The Absolute is fundamentally unknowable and unthinkable in its pure state.

attributions.surface_quote: The Absolute is declared to be unknowable and unthinkable.

canonical_statement: The Absolute manifests as personal forms to facilitate knowledge for the seeker.

attributions.surface_quote: He assumes deified personal aspects to make Himself known to His devotees.

canonical_statement: Individual agency is illusory; all action is performed by the power of the Absolute.

attributions.surface_quote: It is through His power that you live and act.

canonical_statement: The belief in independent individual achievement is a product of ignorance.

attributions.surface_quote: Your idea that this victory is ours is based on ignorance.

canonical_statement: The Absolute is the sole underlying cause of all physical movement and existence.

attributions.surface_quote: Not even a blade of grass can move without His command.

canonical_statement: Spiritual proximity to the Supreme is determined by the degree of purity and direct realization of Truth.

attributions.surface_quote: they were able to do this because they were purer

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality, Brahman, is the sole agent of all action.

attributions.surface_quote: Brahman is the only Doer.

canonical_statement: The absolute reality is formless and cannot be fully contained within any finite manifestation.

attributions.surface_quote: the whole of the unfathomable Brahman could not be seen in any definite form

canonical_statement: The human mind acts as the primary instrument for conceptualizing and approaching the transcendent.

attributions.surface_quote: Only by the mind can the seeker after knowledge approach Brahman

canonical_statement: A purified mind functions as a reflective medium for the manifestation of divine glory.

attributions.surface_quote: when by constant thought of Him the mind becomes purified, then like a polished mirror it can reflect His Divine Glory.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality is a singular, unified source from which all phenomenal existence emerges and into which it eventually dissolves.

attributions.surface_quote: One tremendous Whole becoming the world, and again the world merging in that Whole.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality cannot be perceived by the senses or intellect because it is the foundational consciousness that enables those faculties to function.

attributions.surface_quote: It is the eye of the eye, the ear of the ear... It is beyond the unknown.

canonical_statement: Individual identity is transcended through the realization of one's essential unity with the ultimate source.

attributions.surface_quote: Whoever knows Him in this aspect becomes one with Him.

canonical_statement: The phenomenal world consists of transient forms arising from and returning to an eternal, inexhaustible substrate.

attributions.surface_quote: Bubbles of creation rise on the surface, live for a time, then burst.

canonical_statement: Spiritual liberation is achieved through the purification of the self and the attainment of knowledge regarding the ultimate source.

attributions.surface_quote: He who knows this wisdom... becomes established in the blissful, eternal and highest abode.

canonical_statement: The Supreme Reality is infinite and transcends the capacity for conceptual or objective knowledge.

attributions.surface_quote: The knower of Truth says, 'I know It not,' because he realizes the unbounded nature.

canonical_statement: The Supreme Reality encompasses both the manifest visible world and the unmanifest invisible realm.

attributions.surface_quote: Thou art this, Thou art That, and Thou art all that is beyond.

canonical_statement: True knowledge transcends sensory perception and derives from the Spirit.

attributions.surface_quote: The knowledge of an illumined Sage is not confined to his senses.

canonical_statement: Human mortality is a consequence of the ego identifying with the physical body and mind.

attributions.surface_quote: Mortals become mortals because they fall under the sway of ego.

canonical_statement: The Supreme Reality is the sole agent and source of power for all individual faculties.

attributions.surface_quote: There is no real power, no real doer except God.

canonical_statement: Realizing the Supreme as the underlying substrate of being leads to the transcendence of death.

attributions.surface_quote: When we realize Him as the underlying Reality, we transcend death.

canonical_statement: Spiritual knowledge is transmitted directly from the mind of an illumined teacher to a disciple.

attributions.surface_quote: partaking of the light that streams from the mind of the master

canonical_statement: True wisdom is an inner realization that transcends the literal text of scriptures.

attributions.surface_quote: learning was only a cloak for his inner realization

canonical_statement: The Absolute can be known through a singular, unified knowledge that encompasses all other phenomena.

attributions.surface_quote: What is that, by knowing which everything else becomes known?

canonical_statement: Supreme wisdom is inaccessible through intellectual study, ritual, or moral action, requiring instead meditative purification and renunciation.

attributions.surface_quote: Supreme Wisdom cannot be attained by superficial study... nor by good works.

canonical_statement: The attainment of ultimate truth requires the stripping away of non-essential mental or worldly constructs.

attributions.surface_quote: the Upanishad itself is shorn of all non-essentials

canonical_statement: The Absolute (Brahman) is distinct from the personal creative aspect of Deity (Brahma).

attributions.surface_quote: Brahma is the personal aspect of Deity as distinguished from Brahman, the Absolute.

canonical_statement: There exists a singular, foundational knowledge through which all other knowledge is understood.

attributions.surface_quote: What is that... which being known, all else becomes known?

canonical_statement: Knowledge is categorized into lower, intellectual study and higher, direct vision of the Imperishable.

attributions.surface_quote: There are two kinds of knowledge: higher knowledge and lower knowledge.

canonical_statement: The universe is populated by beings who manifest specific divine qualities and perform creative functions.

attributions.surface_quote: Devas are Bright Beings, each manifesting some special Divine quality.

canonical_statement: Direct experiential knowledge of ultimate reality is superior to theoretical or intellectual knowledge.

attributions.surface_quote: theoretical knowledge must always be inferior to knowledge based on direct experience.

canonical_statement: The ultimate source of existence is unconditioned, imperceptible to senses, and lacks physical attributes.

attributions.surface_quote: That which cannot be seen... which has no origin and no attributes.

canonical_statement: Ultimate realization requires the pacification of sensory, mental, and intellectual faculties.

attributions.surface_quote: It dawns in the soul only when senses, mind and intellect have become pacified.

canonical_statement: The universe emanates from the Imperishable Source, similar to biological growth or secretion.

attributions.surface_quote: does the universe come forth from the Imperishable.

canonical_statement: The creative process of the universe is driven by the internal wisdom and expansion of the Absolute.

attributions.surface_quote: Out of this fire of wisdom... come forth... all forms of material manifestation.

canonical_statement: Knowledge is categorized into a lower form concerning ritual and worldly desire, and a higher form concerning ultimate truth.

attributions.surface_quote: The Vedic teaching is divided into two distinct parts: lower knowledge and higher knowledge.

canonical_statement: Ritual sacrifice serves as a mechanism to test the practitioner's detachment from worldly rewards.

attributions.surface_quote: To test whether his mind is wholly free from desire for earthly rewards.

canonical_statement: The universe contains hierarchical grades of existence, described as seven worlds or heavens.

attributions.surface_quote: The seven worlds represent the rising grades of heavenly pleasure.

canonical_statement: The fire of wisdom is an internal process of refining thoughts, words, and deeds.

attributions.surface_quote: The real fire which every worshipper must light is the fire of wisdom.

canonical_statement: The efficacy of ritual action is contingent upon precise alignment with cosmic and temporal conditions.

attributions.surface_quote: Certain times and conditions were regarded as peculiarly auspicious for performing sacrifice.

canonical_statement: Ritualistic actions and sacrifices are ephemeral and do not lead to ultimate liberation.

attributions.surface_quote: all these sacrifices are inferior and ephemeral.

canonical_statement: Attachment to the fruits of action necessitates continued cycles of birth, death, and suffering.

attributions.surface_quote: after a temporary enjoyment of their heavenly reward fall back again into misery.

canonical_statement: Spiritual ignorance is characterized by the false belief that worldly success or ritual merit is the highest good.

attributions.surface_quote: Regarding sacrifice and good works as the highest aim, these ignorant men know not.

canonical_statement: True spiritual guidance requires direct vision rather than mere intellectual or scriptural learning.

attributions.surface_quote: no one save the man of direct vision shall venture to lead others.

canonical_statement: Finite actions cannot produce permanent results; therefore, heavenly pleasures are temporary and necessitate a return to the cycle of struggle.

attributions.surface_quote: finite actions... cannot be permanent so all heavenly pleasure must come to an end

canonical_statement: All individual beings originate from the Imperishable Being and eventually return to that source.

attributions.surface_quote: thousands of sparks... do the various beings spring forth from the Imperishable and return thither

canonical_statement: The Absolute (Nirguna-Brahman) is infinite, formless, and transcends the need for mind or breath.

attributions.surface_quote: effulgent Being is without form... without breath and without mind

canonical_statement: The Absolute is distinct from and higher than the Creative Energy (Saguna-Brahman) which possesses attributes.

attributions.surface_quote: higher than the High Imperishable... Brahman with attributes, or the personal God

canonical_statement: All manifest existence, including life-force, mind, and elements, originates from the Absolute.

attributions.surface_quote: From Him are born the Prana, mind, all the sense organs, ether, air, fire

canonical_statement: The entire universe and all living beings emanate from and are manifestations of a single, supreme, all-pervading Being.

attributions.surface_quote: All this is Brahman, the Highest Being alone is all.

canonical_statement: The supreme Being resides within the heart of every individual as the inner Self.

attributions.surface_quote: He is the inner Self of all living beings.

canonical_statement: The physical universe, including elements, senses, and biological life, is a direct projection of the supreme Being.

attributions.surface_quote: From Him are born all oceans, mountains and divers rivers.

canonical_statement: Realization of the supreme Being within one's own heart leads to the dissolution of ignorance and the attainment of immortality.

attributions.surface_quote: He who knows this Being dwelling in the cave of the heart cuts asunder ignorance.

canonical_statement: The Supreme Being is the singular, omnipresent substrate of all existence, encompassing both manifest and unmanifest states.

attributions.surface_quote: In Him the whole universe is centered. He is both formful and formless.

canonical_statement: Individual identity (Atman) achieves liberation by merging completely with the Absolute (Brahman) through focused consciousness.

attributions.surface_quote: As the arrow becomes one with the mark, so will he become one with the Supreme.

canonical_statement: The Absolute is beyond the reach of human conceptual understanding and sensory perception.

attributions.surface_quote: Who is beyond the reach of human understanding.

canonical_statement: The sacred sound Om functions as the instrumental bridge or mechanism for directing the soul toward the Absolute.

attributions.surface_quote: The word Om is the bow, the Atman is the arrow.

canonical_statement: Focused attention is a necessary prerequisite for the direct perception of ultimate reality.

attributions.surface_quote: If our mind is divided or scattered we cannot meditate and gain direct perception.

canonical_statement: The individual soul achieves unity with the Supreme through direct knowledge of the Divine.

attributions.surface_quote: The knower of God partakes of His nature.

canonical_statement: The Supreme Being is the fundamental substrate of all manifested existence.

attributions.surface_quote: There can be no form of manifested life apart from Him.

canonical_statement: The Atman resides within the physical heart and is the source of all bodily functions.

attributions.surface_quote: Where the nerves of the body meet... here the Atman dwells.

canonical_statement: The unchanging Soul appears to undergo emotional modifications due to its association with the mind.

attributions.surface_quote: It is unchanging, but It appears to take the modifications of the mind.

canonical_statement: Realization of the Supreme Being dissolves the causal bonds of karma and individual ego.

attributions.surface_quote: When He is seen, the fetters of the heart are broken, and all Karma is destroyed.

canonical_statement: Intellectual analysis is insufficient for the realization of ultimate truth.

attributions.surface_quote: This does not happen when we gain intellectual knowledge only.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality is a self-effulgent light that renders truth self-evident.

attributions.surface_quote: When His light shines in our heart, Truth becomes self-evident.

canonical_statement: Direct perception of the divine light dissolves the causal chains of karma.

attributions.surface_quote: all the chains of Karma past, present and future are shattered.

canonical_statement: The physical universe derives its existence and luminosity from the Supreme Brahman.

attributions.surface_quote: When He shines, everything shines after Him.

canonical_statement: Brahman is omnipresent and constitutes the entirety of the universe.

attributions.surface_quote: The Supreme Brahman alone is the whole Universe.

canonical_statement: The individual self and the Supreme Self coexist within the same being, one acting and one witnessing.

attributions.surface_quote: Two inseparable companions of golden plumage perch on the same tree.

canonical_statement: The individual soul is a reflection of the Supreme Soul, and separation is an illusion caused by the ego.

attributions.surface_quote: The Jiva or individual soul is merely the reflex of the Supreme Soul.

canonical_statement: Individual liberation requires the transcendence of both moral merit and sin, as both function as attachments to the ego.

attributions.surface_quote: sin is an iron chain, so merit can be a golden chain

canonical_statement: The ultimate state of being is characterized by the unification of individual will with the cosmic will.

attributions.surface_quote: mind and will are completely unified with the cosmic mind and will

canonical_statement: The Supreme Reality is simultaneously immanent within the human body and transcendent beyond all sensory perception.

attributions.surface_quote: subtler than the subtlest... yet here (in the body)

canonical_statement: The Self is not accessible through sensory observation or ritual action, but only through a purified mind in meditation.

attributions.surface_quote: not perceived by the eye... when the mind is purified... does the Seer perceive

canonical_statement: The mind is naturally obscured by its entanglement with the senses, but reveals the Self upon purification.

attributions.surface_quote: mind of every creature is interwoven with the senses. When it is purified, then the Self shines forth

canonical_statement: Vital energy (prana) functions as the mediator between the external world and internal mental processes.

attributions.surface_quote: vital energy connects the outer world with the inner

canonical_statement: The soul's true nature is obscured by sense impressions filtered through the mind.

attributions.surface_quote: not until the mind is freed from these obscuring impressions can the soul manifest

canonical_statement: A purified mind achieves alignment with the cosmic will, causing desires to manifest through natural law.

attributions.surface_quote: his desires fulfill themselves by the natural course of law

canonical_statement: Realization of the Self involves recognizing one's essential oneness with the cosmic totality.

attributions.surface_quote: he realizes his oneness with the cosmic life

canonical_statement: The universe is grounded in and sustained by the Supreme Brahman.

attributions.surface_quote: Brahman, in which all this universe rests

canonical_statement: Desire acts as the causal seed for the cycle of birth, death, and suffering.

attributions.surface_quote: Every desire is a seed from which spring birth, death and all mortal afflictions.

canonical_statement: Spiritual liberation is achieved through the cessation of desire and the realization of the Self.

attributions.surface_quote: he whose desires are fulfilled and who has known the Self, his desires vanish

canonical_statement: The realization of the Self is not a product of intellectual effort but a result of divine revelation or selection.

attributions.surface_quote: Self cannot be attained by the study of the Scriptures... He whom the Self chooses

canonical_statement: Spiritual attainment requires the integration of inner vigor, mindfulness, and the renunciation of lower desires.

attributions.surface_quote: Self cannot be attained by one who is devoid of strength, or by one who is unmindful

canonical_statement: The realized soul achieves omnipresence by perceiving the fundamental unity of all existence.

attributions.surface_quote: realizing the all-pervading Spirit present in all things, enter into all.

canonical_statement: At death, the constituent elements of the individual being dissolve back into their universal sources.

attributions.surface_quote: fifteen parts return to their source; the senses go back to their corresponding deities.

canonical_statement: Liberation involves the transcendence of name and form, resulting in union with the universal source.

attributions.surface_quote: As flowing rivers lose themselves in the ocean, giving up name and form.

canonical_statement: Individual consciousness expands into universal consciousness without the annihilation of the true entity.

attributions.surface_quote: consciousness expands into the universal consciousness... he does not lose his true entity.

canonical_statement: Knowledge of the Absolute transforms the knower into the likeness of the Absolute.

attributions.surface_quote: He who knows that highest Brahman becomes like unto Brahman.

canonical_statement: The attainment of metaphysical knowledge requires prior moral and ritual purification of the practitioner.

attributions.surface_quote: only those who have purified themselves... will be able to understand or follow the higher knowledge.

canonical_statement: Metaphysical truth is dangerous or counterproductive to those who lack the necessary spiritual preparation.

attributions.surface_quote: To others it will bring only confusion of mind and impede their progress.
